summary: Assess arid-basin water risks, compare allocation options, and plan adaptation actions. Explore the five-day course and outline.
lede: Water security and climate change planning in arid basins examines how water supply, demand, and climate uncertainty affect basin reliability. It is for water-resource planners, utility professionals, and adaptation specialists who need to assess climate evidence, account for water use, compare allocation scenarios, and screen groundwater and reuse options. Exercises use sample data to develop risk priorities and an adaptation plan with measurable indicators.
audienceIntro: This intermediate course is designed for professionals who work directly with water supply, basin planning, climate adaptation, or water-dependent services and need practical methods for arid-basin decisions.
modules: IPCC Climate Signals for Water Planning
Reuse and Quality in Arid Systems
prerequisites: Prior experience in water resources, water services, climate adaptation, hydrology, irrigation, or environmental planning is expected. No programming is required. Exercises use sample data and Excel; advanced hydrological modelling is introduced at overview level.
topics: Water & wastewater treatment and utility management
